## 固定收益開場論點

6月16日，美國公債上漲。油價再度大跌，帶動通膨補償下降；住宅營建疲弱，加深市場對利率敏感型需求的疑慮；20年期公債增額發行去化良好，也支撐長端表現。2年期殖利率下降1.4個基點至4.055%，5年期下降2.8個基點至4.164%，10年期下降3.5個基點至4.44%，30年期下降3.6個基點至4.944%。2年期與10年期利差收窄2.1個基點至38.5個基點，2年期與30年期利差收窄2.2個基點至88.9個基點。

這波漲勢主要來自通膨補償下降，而非經通膨調整後殖利率明顯下滑。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降3.2個基點至2.306%，10年期實質殖利率僅下降0.3個基點至2.134%。美國與伊朗擬議協議的近最終草案設想立即允許伊朗出售石油、取得至少$3,000億開發基金的資金，並最終解凍遭凍結資產，促使WTI下跌5.82%至$76.05，布蘭特原油下跌5.06%至$78.96。油價一週跌逾13%，一個月跌約28%。

潛在供給改善仍附帶條件。協議預定6月19日簽署，但歐洲官員質疑荷莫茲海峽能否如美國總統Donald Trump所稱迅速重啟，並要求先釐清協議內容，才會承諾參與除雷與巡邏。QatarEnergy預估，安全通行恢復一個月後，液化天然氣產能也只能回復約一半。這些限制未能阻止原油再度重挫，卻凸顯期貨價格迅速重定價與實體能源流量緩慢恢復之間的落差。

美國經濟數據對利率形成相反力量。5月新屋開工月減15.4%，折合年率降至118萬戶，為2020年以來最低，且低於彭博調查中的所有預測。進口價格卻月增1.9%，接近1.0%市場共識的兩倍；燃料進口價格上漲12.5%，非燃料進口價格也廣泛上升0.8%。這些證據增加聯準會在6月17日會議繼續觀望的理由，卻不足以解除通膨警報。

美國公債供給面也強化長天期債券買盤。財政部增額發行$130億、票息5.000%、2046年5月到期的公債，最高得標殖利率為4.927%，投標倍數2.75，高於5月規模較大之新券發行的2.55。間接投標人取得71.57%的競爭性得標額，一級交易商僅承接8.48%。由於沒有發行前交易殖利率可供參照，無法判定標售結果是尾差或低於發行前水準，但較高的投標倍數及偏低的交易商承接比率，顯示這筆規模較小的增額發行獲得終端需求承接。

跨資產收盤表現不像油價持續下跌那樣一致樂觀。標普500指數下跌0.57%，那斯達克100指數下跌1.89%，費城半導體指數重挫5.71%，回吐前一交易日由科技股帶動的部分漲幅。VIX上升1.30%至16.41，美元指數下跌0.09%，黃金近乎持平。投資級債券基金價格微升，高收益及新興市場債券基金則大致持平至微幅走低。因此，在Kevin Warsh以聯準會主席身分主持首次利率決策前，市場呈現名目長天期美債明確上漲、風險偏好卻仍具選擇性的組合。

## 油價舒緩效應延伸至長端

油價進一步下跌，為美國公債市場帶來比美伊最初公布協議時更清晰的通膨降溫訊號。6月15日的早盤漲勢由短端領先，但其後大部分漲幅消退，30年期殖利率終場反而走高。到了週二，10年期與30年期公債表現優於2年期，長端加入漲勢，扭轉部分先前的抗跌反應。

這次走勢的組成至關重要。10年期名目殖利率下降3.5個基點，幾乎全數來自損益兩平通膨率走低，而不是投資人要求的實質利率大幅改變。這種結構反映的是未來能源成本下降，並非市場全面重估基礎成長或均衡政策利率。過去一個月，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降21.5個基點，同期實質殖利率仍上升6.1個基點。

最新版美伊擬議協議進一步說明能源市場為何下修潛在供應短缺的定價。近最終草案將允許伊朗立即出售石油、取得由至少$3,000億資金支持的開發基金，並最終解凍遭凍結資產。不過，這些仍是未來可能實施的條款，並非已完成的石油銷售、融資或資產移轉；雙方仍預定6月19日在瑞士簽署協議。

實際執行的難度高於金融誘因本身所顯示的程度。美國可立即部署的除雷能力有限，因此需要盟友支援。歐洲各國在取得更清楚的協議說明前尚未承諾參與，也不認同Trump所稱海峽可在週五前開放的信心。伊朗與以色列仍就黎巴嫩衝突相互警告，使雙邊協議之外依然存在另一個可能干擾供應的來源。

即使航道重啟，能源生產也無法隨即恢復。QatarEnergy告知買方，安全通行恢復一個月後，產量可回復至約50%的產能。這項時程凸顯央行一直強調的差別：期貨價格可以下降，但數月高昂能源成本、受損基礎設施及航運安排改變所累積的影響不會立即消失。這也說明名目美債的漲勢雖具意義，幅度仍然克制，沒有演變為全面湧向長天期債券的避險行情。

20年期公債標售協助長端守住漲幅。財政部以4.927%的最高得標殖利率接受$130億投標，低於5月發行$160億新券時的5.122%。殖利率差異反映不同的市場水準，但投標數據更直接顯示去化改善：投標倍數由2.55升至2.75，間接投標比率由67.67%升至71.57%，交易商承接比率由9.39%降至8.48%，直接投標人取得19.94%。這批增額發行債券將於6月22日交割，2046年5月15日到期。

交易活動特別集中於涵蓋這批增額發行債券的到期區段。FINRA紀錄的美國公債面額交易量為$1.132兆，較6月15日增加16.5%；名目附息債券交易量增加13.8%至$8,655億。剩餘期限逾10年、但不超過20年的債券交易量激增83.3%至$726億。彙總數據無法判定買賣方向，但交易量集中、標售投標倍數上升與收盤殖利率下降合併來看，顯示長端在吸收大量交易活動的同時仍守住漲勢。

42天期國庫券標售在短端呈現較為混合的結果。財政部以維持不變的3.600%最高得標利率接受$650.01億投標。投標倍數由3.25降至3.12，但間接投標比率由58.67%大幅升至69.06%；直接投標人取得2.17%，交易商承接28.76%，兩者均低於前次標售。國庫券將於6月18日交割、7月30日到期。最高得標利率不變且投標倍數下降，並未顯示整體融資市場受擾；從配售結構來看，即使表面投標倍數降低，需求組成仍有所改善。

因此，殖利率曲線趨平並非只是對成長疲弱的防禦反應。能源相關通膨補償下降、長天期債券標售穩健，加上聯準會決策將至，使5年至30年期區段相對受惠，表現優於對政策較敏感的2年期。短端仍反映高度不確定性：聯準會下一步可能升息、長期維持利率不變，或在勞動市場轉弱時最終降息。

## 進口通膨與房市低迷使聯準會抉擇更複雜

5月進口價格顯示，外部通膨衝擊並不限於燃料。進口價格指數較4月上升1.9%，年增6.7%；前一個月增幅經修正為2.0%，本月數據也高於1.0%的市場共識。燃料進口價格月增12.5%、年增45.1%，但非燃料進口價格同樣月增0.8%、年增3.7%。

出口價格月增1.3%，略高於1.2%的預估；4月增幅修正為3.5%。出口價格年增11.2%，其中農產品及非農產品價格均上升1.2%，顯示漲勢並非集中於單一商品類別。對聯準會而言，這份數據說明早先的能源衝擊已傳導至貿易商品價格，即使原油的未來走勢正在改善。

房市則形成鮮明反向力量。新屋開工月減15.4%，折合年率為118萬戶，降至6年來最低。多戶住宅開工重挫40.2%，構成整體降幅的大部分；獨棟住宅開工也下降1.9%至88.2萬戶。除中西部外，各地區營建活動均下滑；全美最大住宅營建區域南部的開工量降至2020年5月以來最低。

多戶住宅數據一向波動較大。政府公布的90%信賴區間顯示，月變動可能介於下降25.2%與下降5.6%之間。即使考量這項不確定性，整體房市仍然疲弱。高融資成本壓抑買方需求，促使建商降價、補貼房貸利率並減少投機性營建。整體建築許可月減0.7%，折合年率為141萬戶，但獨棟住宅許可小幅增加。

這組數據既不是明確的緊縮訊號，也不足以支持近期降息。進口價格進一步證明，戰爭相關能源成本及供應中斷已擴散至商品；房市則顯示，限制性的借貸成本正在利率敏感產業造成可見損害。油價下跌改善未來通膨路徑，卻無法逆轉5月已實現的進口成本上升，也無法確定其中多少會轉嫁至消費者價格。

市場普遍預期聯準會將把利率維持在3.50%至3.75%，但經濟學家與交易員對後續政策嚴重分歧。Citadel Securities的Frank Flight認為，寬鬆的金融情勢、持續的供應中斷、轉強的勞動市場及龐大的人工智慧投資，可能維持廣泛的通膨壓力。他認為9月、12月及2027年3月升息的風險正在增加，並預期聯準會預測的分布會比市場定價更偏鷹派。

花旗集團美國首席經濟學家Andrew Hollenhorst則持相反看法。他預期政策聲明將移除寬鬆傾向，預測也會顯示今年不降息；但若未來數月勞動市場轉弱，他仍預測自9月起降息三次。若沒有這種惡化，降息可能延至2027年。他的論點部分建立在能源價格下跌可讓聯準會忽略部分通膨壓力之上。

選擇權市場反映這項分歧，並未給出明確答案。交易員幾乎確信6月利率不變，但部位涵蓋年底前升息超過一次，到2027年上半年降息等多種結果。近期部分交易押注首次完整升息要到1月才會發生，另一些則尋求長端債券遭拋售時的保護。市場對Warsh的反應函數經驗有限，加上他偏好較少細節的央行溝通，使預期分散程度進一步擴大。

這種可能的溝通轉變，無論下一步政策利率方向為何，都會獨立影響利率市場。Warsh就任主席前曾批評聯準會指引過於頻繁且具體，因此市場開始考慮聲明縮短、記者會減少，以及經濟預測摘要可能調整。高盛估計，聯準會長期轉向更清晰溝通的過程，已使10年期期限溢價下降約5個基點。即使聯邦基金利率預測變化不大，若突然減少溝通，部分不確定性溢價仍可能回升。

美國公債收盤走勢呈現這些相互競爭的力量。2年期殖利率雖然下降，幅度卻小於中長天期。隨油價下跌，投資人願意下修部分通膨補償，也在標售後增持長天期債券，但並未排除聯準會維持或強化緊縮傾向的可能性。因此，6月17日決策即將到來之際，市場信心偏低；儘管維持利率不變幾乎已成定局，民間預測的分布卻異常廣泛。

## 日本央行升息，但日圓與長天期債券對步調存疑

日本央行將政策利率調升25個基點至1%，為1995年以來最高，並表示若經濟發展符合展望，將繼續升息。表決結果為7票對1票，理事Toichiro Asada反對升息。由於決定符合市場普遍預期，焦點轉向後續緊縮速度及日本央行債券購買計畫的未來。

日本央行強調，原油成本居高不下，已迅速傳導至企業間交易，並可能擴散至更廣泛的消費者價格。配合中長期通膨預期上升，基礎通膨可能超過2%目標。行長Kazuo Ueda因住院缺席，由副行長Shinichi Uchida代為出席；Uchida表示，日本央行將繼續調整貨幣寬鬆程度，並監控匯率對物價的影響。

政策指引足以維持市場對進一步正常化的預期，緊迫性卻不足以顯著提振日圓。記者會後，日圓約在160.35兌1美元交易，決策公布前一度升至約160.05。Uchida表示，難以判斷利率還需升至多高；策略師認為，其說法符合循序漸進、而非加速緊縮的路徑。隔夜交換市場定價顯示，10月前再度升息的機率約為54%。

日本公債反應更為明顯。10年期與20年期殖利率均上升7個基點，其他天期也走高，反映投資人衡量後續升息及民間市場必須承接的長天期債券規模。日圓疲弱加深疑慮：即使日本央行已升息，美日利差依然很大，而日圓在160附近也使進一步干預匯市的可能性持續受到關注。

日本央行另表示，自2027年4月起將停止削減每月購債額，並維持在約¥2兆。這接近2013年大規模刺激政策啟動前的速度，遠低於2023年1月¥23.7兆的高峰。這項變更終止主動逐步減少購債的安排，卻不代表日本央行持債規模將凍結；隨證券到期，資產負債表仍可持續縮減。

這項決策試圖把利率正常化與公債市場可避免的動盪分開處理。日本央行可在調高政策利率的同時維持可預測的購債速度，讓持債透過到期償還自然下降，而非加快裁量性減持。這種做法降低長天期債券投資人的一項不確定性，但無法取代民間需求；政府發債及央行持債到期後釋出的供給仍須由市場承接。

政治限制仍不容忽視。首相Sanae Takaichi偏好寬鬆政策，由她任命的Asada也是本次唯一的反對票。另一名支持再通膨政策的任命人選Ayano Sato將於6月底加入理事會，兩名立場鮮明的鷹派理事則將在2027年任期屆滿。目前多數理事支持正常化，但未來成員組成可能使政策路徑不像聲明中的通膨警告所暗示的那樣直線發展。

整套政策從利率水準與方向來看偏鷹派，執行方式卻相當謹慎。1%的利率、7票對1票的表決結果，以及對通膨超越目標的明確憂慮，都支持進一步緊縮。然而，日圓反應有限、長期殖利率上升，且日本央行仍將金融情勢形容為寬鬆，說明市場為何懷疑其行動速度是否足以迅速穩定通膨預期與匯率。

## 中國走弱，歐洲勞動市場訊號分歧

中國5月數據顯示，由出口與科技帶動的生產，和疲弱的家庭及民間部門需求之間差距擴大。零售銷售年減0.6%，為2022年底經濟解除疫情限制後首次下滑；汽車購買量下降16%，今年前5個月固定資產投資萎縮4.1%，民間資本支出下降7.1%，創2020年以來最差表現。

製造業投資6年來首次下滑，房地產低迷也持續打擊信心與家庭財富。70個城市新屋價格繼前月下降0.19%後，5月再月減0.2%，低線城市尤其疲弱。上市開發商指數一度下跌3%，回到2024年9月刺激措施啟動前的水準；今年以來，該房地產指數已下跌近14%。

工業生產增速卻由4.1%加快至4.5%，主要受出口及人工智慧相關硬體支撐，高科技製造業增加值上升15%。這種反差顯示，中國仍能創造工業產出，消費、房地產及廣泛民間投資卻未同步復甦。這樣的組合維持貨幣或財政支援壓力，但企業與家庭仍不願借貸及支出，也使政策傳導更加困難。

離岸主權債發行則對香港融資市場產生更直接影響。中國財政部發行人民幣150億元債券，其中包括人民幣45億元、票息創歷史新低1.29%的2年期債券。這筆最長期限達10年的多券種交易獲3.86倍認購。強勁需求伴隨離岸人民幣融資成本上升，包括1個月期利率升至兩個月高點；在季末監管要求到來前，流動性原已趨緊，這次發債又進一步抽走資金。

歐洲勞動市場數據對歐洲央行釋出的訊號較不劇烈，但同樣分歧。歐元區第1季每小時勞動成本年增3.2%，低於3.3%的市場共識及第4季經修正後的3.4%。工資與薪資上升3.4%，非工資成本上升2.9%。商業經濟中，營建業增幅最快，達4.1%；工業與服務業分別為3.3%與3.1%。

職缺率由前一季的2.2%升至2.3%，但仍低於一年前的2.4%。歐盟整體職缺率維持2.1%，一年前為2.2%；服務業職缺率為2.4%，工業與營建業均為2.0%。因此，勞動需求較前季穩定至略為轉強，卻未扭轉過去一年可見的降溫趨勢。

歐洲央行官員持續主張，荷莫茲海峽即使按計畫重啟，也無法迅速消除已在傳導途中的通膨。首席經濟學家Philip Lane表示，能源價格連續四個月處於高檔，可能使通膨升破3%，間接影響並將延伸至明年的食品、商品與服務價格。他認為約$80至$81的石油遠期曲線遠低於不利情境，但尚未回到戰前水準。

管理委員會成員Jose Luis Escriva與Gabriel Makhlouf分別強調，生產、航運及供應鏈恢復仍有不確定性。他們的談話為較溫和的工資數據提供背景：勞動成本增速放緩，降低一項通膨持續性來源，卻無法消除能源與供給衝擊的滯後效應，而這些效應正是歐洲央行近期升息的理由。職缺數據也尚未顯示勞動需求崩落。

瑞典與挪威則從不同的經濟條件出發迎接利率決策。市場預期瑞典央行將利率維持在1.75%；瑞典通膨低於目標且失業率偏高，容許央行繼續觀望，但進口價格風險可能使其預測路徑上移。挪威央行繼5月升息後，預料將利率維持在4.25%，不過通膨黏著使這項判斷不如瑞典明確。兩國雖同樣面對能源價格下降的前景，瑞典內需疲弱與挪威通膨持續之間的差異依舊存在。

在美國固定收益市場截點之後，智利央行連續第4次會議一致決議將利率維持在4.5%。央行表示，隨需求轉弱且燃料價格衝擊仍受控制，通膨風險已更接近平衡，但也警告石油供應尚未正常化。央行將2026年經濟成長預測由1.5%至2.5%下修至1%至1.75%。由於決策在美國公債交易時段結束後才公布，未影響6月16日的美國殖利率走勢。

## 初級市場仍暢通，受壓借款人爭取時間

主權及企業發行人持續找到融資窗口，但表現最強的交易均有明確資金用途，並搭配稀缺性或明確讓利。菲律賓透過2026年第2次、也是最後一次國際債券發行籌得$250億。認購訂單達發行額的4.4倍後，交易規模由最初的$200億上調。

這筆三券種美元債包括增額發行一批1月發行的$30億債券。新發行10年期債券的定價為美國公債殖利率加92.5個基點，初步詢價約為加125個基點；5.5年期債券的利差定為55個基點，初步定價指引則接近85個基點。政府表示，這筆交易已完成全年外部商業借款計畫。

美伊可能達成協議所帶來的風險偏好改善有利於這筆交易，但也突顯菲律賓境外與境內融資成本的差距。菲律賓標售7年期公債時，平均殖利率上升13.6個基點至6.779%；財政部近期也曾在國內標售中拒絕投標，以抑制借款成本。即使菲律賓全年整體借款計畫仍高達2.68兆披索，這筆美元債仍讓馬尼拉得以取得相對較低的定價。

STMicroelectronics利用今年以來股價上漲200%的機會，取得成本較低的股權連結融資。這家晶片製造商計畫發行兩批、合計$150億的可轉換公司債，分別於2031年與2033年到期。公司擬以部分募集資金贖回2027年到期的$75億零息債券，其餘用於一般企業用途。

2031年到期債券的票息行銷區間為0%至0.5%，轉換溢價為47.5%至52.5%；2033年到期債券的擬議票息為0.625%至1.125%，轉換溢價為50%至55%。由於STMicro股價已升破$45.10的轉換價格，再融資2027年債券也能處理股權稀釋風險。這筆交易延續可轉債發行潮：投入資料中心與人工智慧投資的企業，正藉此取得低於普通公司債的現金票息。

並非所有融資發展都反映市場資金充裕。隨印尼政府公債、印尼盾及政策預期劇烈波動，印尼公司債波動率升至4年最高。最高評級公司債的30天年化波動率升至23%。今年以來，印尼盾公司債發行量仍以76.8兆印尼盾創新高，成長約11%，但分析師預期部分發行人將縮減交易規模，或等待定價較穩定後再進場。

前一週內，5年期AAA公司債利差曾在不同交易日擴大或收窄逾10個基點。即使基礎信用品質沒有改變，這種波動仍使借款人與基金難以就相對政府公債的成交溢酬達成共識。隨印尼盾走弱，當地債券市場的重要性上升；即使發債活動沒有停止，較高的票息仍可能抑制投資與消費。

Optimum Communications的重整爭議顯示，法律與稅務架構可能凌駕傳統估值因素。公司警告債權人，若強制其CSC Holdings子公司進入止贖程序，或要求進行債轉股，可能因不再納入合併報表而觸發逾$400億稅務負債。Optimum整體債務約$260億，其中CSC的借款逾$200億。

Optimum提出協商重整方案，由CSC債權人取得母公司股權；公司表示，這種安排可降低稅務成本。債權人仍在評估所稱稅務負債是否可信，顧問已獲准檢視相關分析。爭議也反映在債券價格上：$10億、票息7.5%、2028年到期的債券週二下跌逾3美分至26美分；$21億、票息11.75%、2029年到期的債券則穩定在略高於60美分，兩個月前一度在75美分附近交易。

Brightline Trains Florida取得的喘息空間較為有限。$9.85億、票息12%的市政債持有人同意把原定週一支付的款項延至6月底，並豁免一項違約：公司未經債權人同意，於5月21日新增$2.22億借款。據知情人士透露，承保逾$10億Brightline優先債券的Assured Guaranty提供了這筆營運資金貸款。

延期後，眼前期限移至7月1日附近，屆時另有$22億優先債務及$11億公司票據須支付票息。Brightline在自行設定的期限前未能找到買方，其後開始考慮破產融資方案。因此，新資金與豁免只是為協商式負債管理爭取時間，並未解決$55億債務負擔；支撐這些債務的乘客收入與獲利，均遠低於先前預測。

另一筆附條件融資則顯示美國政府在戰略供應鏈中的角色擴大。稀土精煉商Phoenix Tailings取得五角大廈提供的$50億附條件貸款，用於一座擬於2028年前生產多種稀土材料的工廠。這項承諾在交割前仍須完成財務、法律與技術盡職調查。連同能源部近期核發的$6.6億補助，資金將支持降低對中國加工產能依賴的計畫，但這筆貸款目前尚未撥付。

因此，當日信用市場證據具有選擇性，並非全面強勁或普遍疲弱。菲律賓與STMicro把握有利市況，以改善後的條件取得大額資金；印尼發行量雖創今年新高，發行人仍面對價格劇烈波動；Optimum在重整談判中以具爭議的稅務後果作為籌碼，Brightline債權人則以暫緩立即執法換取更多協商時間。這些差異，比廣泛信用債基金的單日小幅波動更具意義。

## 前瞻市場意義

美國市場近期焦點是6月17日美東時間08:30公布的5月零售銷售。繼4月成長0.5%後，整體銷售預估增加0.4%至0.6%；扣除汽車與汽油的銷售預估增加0.3%，控制組預估成長0.4%。若數據強勁，將與房市低迷形成對比，並支持消費能承受限制性利率的看法；若數據疲弱，則會在聯準會決策前擴大內需降溫的證據。

FOMC將於美東時間14:00公布決策，Warsh於14:30舉行就任後首場會後記者會。市場普遍預期目標區間維持3.50%至3.75%。真正足以推動市場的資訊，將是利率預測的分布、先前寬鬆傾向如何處理，以及Warsh如何權衡已實現的商品通膨與油價下降帶來的未來舒緩。即使政策利率預測路徑不變，指引形式或資訊量的任何調整，也可能獨立影響期限溢價。

英國6月17日稍早公布消費者物價。繼前月月增0.7%、年增2.8%後，整體通膨預估月增0.4%、年增3.0%。這是英格蘭銀行6月18日決策前最後一項主要通膨資訊，市場預期利率維持3.75%。表決票數與政策指引將顯示，官員更重視經濟活動疲弱及油價下跌，還是能源衝擊已造成的通膨預期與滯後價格效應。

歐元區最終通膨數據預料將確認5月初值：整體通膨3.2%，核心通膨2.5%。市場將把結果與每小時勞動成本增速放緩至3.2%，以及職缺率較前季小幅上升一併解讀。若初值獲得確認，歐洲央行仍須在較溫和的工資訊號與官員警告之間權衡；後者認為食品、商品及服務通膨將繼續吸收先前能源成本的影響。

瑞典央行將於6月17日決策，預期利率維持1.75%；挪威央行則在6月18日公布決定，預料將維持4.25%。瑞典更新後的利率路徑將顯示，即使國內情勢疲弱，輸入型通膨是否足以使未來升息時點提前。挪威的政策路徑則有助判斷5月升息是一次性應對，還是一連串後續行動的開端。

6月18日還有印尼央行、瑞士央行、英格蘭銀行及菲律賓央行公布決策。印尼與菲律賓預料都將考慮再升息25個基點，瑞士央行則預估維持0.00%。匯率穩定、國內需求及能源價格傳導速度各不相同，使這些決策的差異大於油價普遍下跌所暗示的程度。

美國財政部將於6月18日美東時間11:30標售$700億4週期國庫券及$750億8週期國庫券，並於13:00增額發行$240億、票息1.250%、2031年4月到期的5年期TIPS。這筆抗通膨債券標售安排在聯準會預測公布後，也緊接6月16日10年期損益兩平通膨率下降3.2個基點、實質殖利率幾乎未動的交易日。投標及配售結果將直接檢驗油價帶動重定價後，市場對實質殖利率與通膨保護的需求。

美國6月18日公布的初領失業救濟金人數，將更新近期新申請人數升至22.9萬、續領人數升至179.5萬的趨勢是否逐漸持續。勞動市場數據是兩派觀點分歧的核心：一方預期最終降息，另一方則認為就業仍具韌性、金融情勢寬鬆且通膨廣泛，將迫使聯準會升息。

日本將於6月19日公布5月全國消費者物價，排除生鮮食品的通膨率預估維持年增1.4%。這是日本央行升息後首份全國通膨數據，將檢驗央行關於油價傳導與通膨預期可能推升基礎通膨至目標以上的警告，也有助市場判斷10月前再次升息是否合理。

美伊擬議協議同樣預定6月19日簽署，SIFMA則建議當日美國固定收益市場全天休市。假期將延後市場針對最終條款、盟友參與除雷，以及航運恢復時程的國內價格發現。能源市場真正的考驗不只是協議簽署，而是安全通行、生產與出口量能否依目前較低油價所反映的時程恢復。

overall_summary.headline: 油價舒緩壓低通膨補償，美國公債上漲
overall_summary.session_narrative:
6月16日美國公債上漲，2年期殖利率下降1.4個基點至4.055%，5年期下降2.8個基點至4.164%，10年期下降3.5個基點至4.44%，30年期下降3.6個基點至4.944%。2年期與10年期利差收窄至38.5個基點，2年期與30年期利差收窄至88.9個基點。

長端走勢幾乎完全由通膨補償下降帶動。WTI下跌5.82%，布蘭特原油下跌5.06%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降3.2個基點至2.306%，10年期實質殖利率則僅下降0.3個基點至2.134%。美伊近最終協議設想立即允許伊朗出售石油，但預定6月19日簽署的協議，仍未確定安全通行、生產與出口何時恢復。

美國數據使政策前景更為複雜。新屋開工重挫15.4%，折合年率降至118萬戶；進口價格則上升1.9%，其中非燃料進口價格廣泛上漲0.8%。$130億20年期公債增額發行的投標倍數改善，交易商承接比率偏低，協助長天期債券守住漲幅。股市下跌，半導體類股跌勢尤其明顯，波動率也上升；在Kevin Warsh以聯準會主席身分主持首次利率決策前，風險偏好仍具選擇性。
overall_summary.summary: 原油再度大跌，壓低通膨補償；住宅營建疲弱，加深市場對利率敏感型需求的疑慮；20年期公債增額發行去化良好，也支撐長端，帶動美國公債上漲、殖利率曲線趨平。不過，進口價格廣泛上升，仍未讓聯準會解除通膨警報。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied on June 16 as another sharp fall in oil pulled inflation compensation lower, weak housing construction reinforced concern about rate-sensitive demand and a well-absorbed 20-year reopening supported the long end. The 2-year yield declined 1.4 basis points to 4.055%, the 5-year fell 2.8 basis points to 4.164%, the 10-year dropped 3.5 basis points to 4.44% and the 30-year declined 3.6 basis points to 4.944%. The move flattened 2s10s by 2.1 basis points to 38.5 basis points and 2s30s by 2.2 basis points to 88.9 basis points.

The rally was driven much more by lower inflation compensation than by a decline in inflation-adjusted yields. The 10-year breakeven fell 3.2 basis points to 2.306%, while the 10-year real yield slipped only 0.3 basis point to 2.134%. WTI dropped 5.82% to $76.05 and Brent fell 5.06% to $78.96 as a near-final draft of the proposed US-Iran agreement contemplated immediate Iranian oil sales, access to a $300 billion development fund and an eventual release of frozen assets. Oil was down more than 13% over the week and about 28% over the month.

The prospective supply relief remained conditional. The agreement is scheduled to be signed June 19, but European officials questioned whether the Strait of Hormuz could reopen as quickly as President Donald Trump suggested and sought clarity before committing to demining and patrol operations. QatarEnergy expected to restore only about half of its liquefied-natural-gas capacity one month after safe passage resumes. Those details did not prevent another large fall in crude, but they separated the rapid repricing of futures from the slower work of restoring physical energy flows.

US economic releases pulled rates in opposite directions. Housing starts plunged 15.4% in May to a 1.18 million annualized rate, the lowest since 2020 and below every forecast in a Bloomberg survey. Import prices, however, rose 1.9% on the month, almost twice the 1.0% consensus, with a 12.5% increase in fuel accompanied by a broad 0.8% rise in nonfuel imports. The evidence gave the Federal Reserve more reason to wait at its June 17 decision, but not an inflation all-clear.

Treasury supply strengthened the duration bid. The $13 billion reopening of the 5.000% bond due May 2046 stopped at 4.927%, with a 2.75 bid-to-cover ratio compared with 2.55 at May’s larger new issue. Indirect bidders took 71.57% of accepted competitive tenders and primary dealers only 8.48%. With no when-issued reference available, the stop cannot be characterized as a tail or through, but the stronger cover and low dealer share showed that the smaller reopening found end demand.

The cross-asset close was less uniformly optimistic than the continued decline in oil. The S&P 500 fell 0.57%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.89% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index dropped 5.71%, reversing part of the previous session’s technology-led advance. The VIX rose 1.30% to 16.41, while the dollar index slipped 0.09% and gold was nearly unchanged. Investment-grade bond-fund prices edged higher, but high-yield and emerging-market debt funds were little changed to slightly lower. The session therefore combined a clear rally in nominal duration with a more selective appetite for risk ahead of Kevin Warsh’s first Fed decision as chair.

## Oil Relief Reaches the Long End

The further decline in oil gave the Treasury market a cleaner disinflation signal than it had received after the initial US-Iran announcement. On June 15, the front end had led an early rally before much of the move faded and the 30-year yield finished higher. On Tuesday, the 10- and 30-year sectors outperformed the 2-year, bringing long duration into the rally and reversing some of that resistance.

The composition of the move was important. Almost all of the 3.5-basis-point decline in the 10-year nominal yield came from lower breakeven inflation, not a large change in the real rate investors demanded. That pattern was consistent with cheaper prospective energy rather than a wholesale reassessment of underlying growth or the equilibrium policy rate. The 10-year breakeven was down 21.5 basis points over a month, while the real yield remained 6.1 basis points higher over the same period.

The latest version of the proposed US-Iran accord supplied more detail about why energy markets were marking down the prospective shortage. A near-final draft would permit Iran to sell oil immediately, provide access to a development fund financed with at least $300 billion and eventually release frozen assets. The terms were prospective rather than completed sales, financing or asset transfers, and the two sides were still expected to sign the agreement in Switzerland on June 19.

Implementation remained more difficult than the financial incentives alone suggested. The US needs allied support for mine clearance because its readily deployable demining capacity is limited. European governments had not committed without a clearer account of the agreement, and they disputed Trump’s confidence that the strait could be open by Friday. Iran and Israel also continued to exchange warnings over the conflict in Lebanon, leaving another possible source of disruption outside the bilateral accord.

Energy production cannot be restored merely by reopening the shipping lane. QatarEnergy told buyers that output could recover to about 50% of capacity a month after safe passage is restored. That timetable reinforced the distinction central banks have been making between a lower futures price and the accumulated effect of months of expensive energy, damaged infrastructure and altered shipping arrangements. It also explained why the nominal Treasury rally was meaningful but remained measured rather than becoming a broad flight into duration.

The 20-year auction helped the long end retain its gains. Treasury accepted $13 billion at a 4.927% high yield, down from 5.122% at the $16 billion May new issue. The comparison in yields reflects different market levels, but the bidding statistics showed a more direct improvement in absorption: cover increased to 2.75 from 2.55, indirect participation rose to 71.57% from 67.67% and the dealer share declined to 8.48% from 9.39%. Direct bidders took 19.94%. The reopened bond settles June 22 and matures May 15, 2046.

Trading activity was especially heavy around the maturity sector containing the reopened security. FINRA recorded $1.132 trillion of Treasury par activity, 16.5% more than on June 15, while nominal-coupon activity increased 13.8% to $865.5 billion. Activity in securities with more than 10 and no more than 20 years remaining surged 83.3% to $72.6 billion. The aggregates do not identify buyer direction, but the concentration of turnover, the stronger auction cover and the closing yield decline together show that the long end absorbed substantial activity without giving up the rally.

The 42-day bill auction produced a more mixed front-end result. Treasury accepted $65.001 billion at an unchanged 3.600% high rate. Bid-to-cover slipped to 3.12 from 3.25, but indirect participation rose sharply to 69.06% from 58.67%; direct bidders took 2.17% and dealers 28.76%, both lower than at the previous auction. The bills settle June 18 and mature July 30. The unchanged stop and smaller cover did not indicate a generalized funding disturbance, while the allocation showed that the composition of demand improved despite the lower headline ratio.

The curve’s flattening was therefore not simply a defensive response to weak growth. Lower energy-related inflation compensation, a solid long-duration auction and the approaching Fed decision all favored the 5- to 30-year sectors relative to the policy-sensitive 2-year. The front end still reflected meaningful uncertainty about whether the Fed’s next move would be an increase, a prolonged hold or, under a weaker labor scenario, an eventual cut.

## Import Inflation and a Housing Slump Complicate the Fed’s Choice

May import prices showed that the external inflation impulse was broader than fuel. The index rose 1.9% from April and 6.7% from a year earlier. The monthly increase followed a revised 2.0% advance and exceeded the 1.0% consensus. Fuel-import prices surged 12.5% on the month and 45.1% from a year earlier, but nonfuel imports also rose 0.8% and were 3.7% higher over 12 months.

Export prices increased 1.3% on the month, slightly above the 1.2% estimate, after a revised 3.5% rise in April. They were 11.2% higher than a year earlier. Agricultural and nonagricultural export prices each advanced 1.2%, giving the report breadth beyond one commodity category. For the Fed, the release showed that the earlier energy shock had already reached traded-goods prices even as the prospective path of crude was improving.

Housing supplied a pronounced counterweight. Starts fell 15.4% to a 1.18 million annualized pace, their weakest level in 6 years. Multifamily construction plunged 40.2%, accounting for most of the headline decline, but single-family starts also fell 1.9% to 882,000. Construction declined in every region except the Midwest, and starts in the South, the largest homebuilding region, fell to their lowest since May 2020.

The multifamily data are volatile: the government’s 90% confidence interval placed the monthly change between a 25.2% decline and a 5.6% drop. Even allowing for that uncertainty, the broader housing picture remained soft. Builders were cutting prices, subsidizing mortgage rates and reducing speculative construction as high financing costs restrained buyers. Total permits declined 0.7% to a 1.41 million annualized rate, although single-family permits edged higher.

The combination left the Fed facing neither a straightforward tightening signal nor a case for near-term easing. Import prices added to evidence that war-related energy costs and supply disruptions had broadened into goods. Housing showed that restrictive borrowing costs were producing visible damage in a rate-sensitive sector. Falling oil improved the future inflation path, but it did not reverse May’s realized increase in import costs or establish how much of it would reach consumer prices.

Economists and traders were sharply divided over what should follow the widely expected hold at 3.50%-3.75%. Citadel Securities’ Frank Flight argued that easy financial conditions, lingering supply disruptions, a strengthening labor market and heavy artificial-intelligence investment could sustain broad inflation. He saw increasing risk of rate increases in September, December and March 2027 and expected the Fed’s projections to show a more hawkish distribution than market pricing.

Citigroup chief US economist Andrew Hollenhorst took the opposite view. He expected the policy statement to remove its easing bias and the projections to show no cuts this year, but retained a forecast for three reductions beginning in September if the labor market weakened over the following months. Without that deterioration, he said the cuts could be delayed until 2027. His case rested partly on the decline in energy prices creating room for the Fed to look through some of the inflation pressure.

Options markets reflected that disagreement rather than resolving it. Traders treated an unchanged June decision as nearly certain, but positioned for outcomes ranging from more than one increase by year-end to reductions during the first half of 2027. Some recent trades targeted the first full hike only in January, while others sought protection against a long-end bond selloff. The dispersion was amplified by limited experience with Warsh’s reaction function and his preference for less detailed central-bank communication.

That prospective communication shift carries a rates implication independent of the direction of the next policy move. Warsh had criticized the frequency and specificity of Fed guidance before becoming chair, raising questions about shorter statements, fewer press conferences and possible changes to the Summary of Economic Projections. Goldman Sachs estimated that the long transition toward clearer communication had reduced the 10-year term premium by about 5 basis points. Pulling back abruptly could return some uncertainty premium even if the funds-rate forecast itself changed little.

The Treasury close captured these competing forces. The 2-year yield declined, but by less than intermediate and long maturities. Investors were willing to mark down some inflation compensation as oil fell and to own duration after the auction, yet they did not remove the possibility that the Fed could retain or strengthen a tightening bias. The June 17 decision therefore approached with a low-conviction market and an unusually wide range of private forecasts around a nearly certain hold.

## The BOJ Tightens, but the Yen and Long Bonds Question the Pace

The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1%, the highest since 1995, and said it would continue increasing rates if the economy evolved in line with its outlook. The vote was 7-1, with board member Toichiro Asada opposing the increase. The decision was widely anticipated, shifting attention toward the pace of subsequent tightening and the future of the BOJ’s bond purchases.

The central bank emphasized the risk that elevated crude costs had already moved rapidly through business-to-business transactions and could spread to a wider set of consumer prices. Combined with rising medium- and long-term inflation expectations, it warned that underlying inflation could move above the 2% target. Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida, standing in for hospitalized Governor Kazuo Ueda, said the bank would continue to adjust the degree of monetary accommodation and monitor the impact of the exchange rate on prices.

The guidance was forceful enough to preserve expectations for further normalization, but not urgent enough to strengthen the yen materially. The currency traded around 160.35 per dollar after the briefing, having reached about 160.05 before the decision. Uchida said it was difficult to know how much further rates would need to rise, and strategists interpreted his presentation as consistent with a gradual path rather than acceleration. Overnight swaps assigned about a 54% probability to another increase by October.

Japanese government bonds reacted more clearly. The 10- and 20-year yields rose 7 basis points, with other maturities also higher, as investors weighed further rate increases and the amount of duration the private market must absorb. The weak yen added to the concern: the interest-rate differential with the US remained wide even after the hike, and levels around 160 kept the possibility of further foreign-exchange intervention in view.

The BOJ also said that from April 2027 it would stop reducing its monthly bond purchases and maintain them at roughly ¥2 trillion. That is close to the pace before the launch of the central bank’s large-scale stimulus in 2013 and far below the January 2023 peak of ¥23.7 trillion. The change ends the active step-down in purchases, but it does not freeze the BOJ’s holdings; the balance sheet can continue shrinking as securities mature.

The decision attempted to separate rate normalization from avoidable instability in the government-bond market. The BOJ can raise its policy rate while maintaining a predictable purchase pace, allowing holdings to decline through redemptions instead of faster discretionary reductions. That approach reduces one source of uncertainty for long-duration investors without replacing the private demand needed to absorb government issuance and maturing central-bank holdings.

Political constraints remain relevant. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has expressed a preference for accommodative policy, and Asada, whom she appointed, supplied the sole dissent. Another reflationist appointee, Ayano Sato, is due to join the board at the end of June, while the terms of two prominent hawks expire in 2027. The board’s current majority supports normalization, but its future composition could make the path less linear than the statement’s inflation warning implied.

The result was a policy package that looked hawkish in level and direction but cautious in execution. A 1% rate, a 7-1 vote and explicit concern about inflation above target all supported further tightening. The muted yen response, higher long-term yields and continued accommodative characterization of financial conditions showed why markets remain uncertain that the BOJ is moving quickly enough to stabilize inflation expectations and the currency.

## China Weakens as Europe’s Labor Signals Point in Different Directions

China’s May data showed a widening gap between export- and technology-led production and weak household and private-sector demand. Retail sales fell 0.6% from a year earlier, the first decline since the economy reopened from pandemic restrictions in late 2022. Car purchases dropped 16%, fixed-asset investment contracted 4.1% in the first 5 months of the year and private capital expenditure fell 7.1%, its worst performance since 2020.

Manufacturing investment declined for the first time in 6 years, while the property downturn continued to weigh on confidence and household wealth. New-home prices across 70 cities fell 0.2% from April after a 0.19% decline, with lower-tier cities remaining especially weak. A gauge of listed developers fell as much as 3% and returned to levels seen before the September 2024 stimulus campaign. The property gauge was down nearly 14% for the year.

Industrial production nevertheless accelerated to 4.5% from 4.1%, supported by exports and artificial-intelligence-related hardware. High-technology manufacturing value added rose 15%. The contrast left China capable of generating industrial output without a comparable recovery in consumption, property or broad private investment. That mix preserves pressure for monetary or fiscal support but also complicates transmission when firms and households remain reluctant to borrow and spend.

Offshore sovereign issuance created a more immediate funding effect in Hong Kong. China’s Ministry of Finance sold 15 billion yuan of bonds, including 4.5 billion yuan of 2-year debt at a record-low 1.29% coupon. The multi-tranche deal, which extended to 10 years, was 3.86 times subscribed. Strong demand coincided with a rise in offshore yuan funding costs, including the 1-month rate reaching a 2-month high, as the sale drained liquidity already tightening ahead of quarter-end regulatory requirements.

Europe’s labor releases offered a less dramatic but still mixed signal for the European Central Bank. Euro-area hourly labor costs rose 3.2% from a year earlier in Q1, below the 3.3% consensus and a revised 3.4% pace in Q4. Wages and salaries increased 3.4%, while non-wage costs rose 2.9%. Construction had the fastest increase within the business economy at 4.1%, compared with 3.3% in industry and 3.1% in services.

The job-vacancy rate rose to 2.3% from 2.2% in the prior quarter but remained below the 2.4% rate a year earlier. The EU-wide rate held at 2.1%, compared with 2.2% a year ago. Services vacancies stood at 2.4%, while industry and construction were at 2.0%. Labor demand therefore looked stable to slightly firmer sequentially, without reversing the cooling visible over the year.

ECB officials continued to argue that the proposed Hormuz reopening would not quickly erase the inflation already in the pipeline. Chief Economist Philip Lane said four months of elevated energy prices were likely to push inflation above 3%, with indirect effects reaching food, goods and services into next year. He judged oil’s forward curve around $80-$81 as well below adverse scenarios but not a return to prewar levels.

Governing Council members Jose Luis Escriva and Gabriel Makhlouf separately stressed uncertainty over restored production, shipping and supply chains. Their comments placed the softer wage reading in context: slower labor-cost growth reduces one source of persistence, but it does not remove the lagged energy and supply effects that motivated the ECB’s recent increase. The vacancy data also stopped short of signaling a collapse in labor demand.

Sweden and Norway were approaching their decisions from different starting points. The Riksbank was expected to hold at 1.75%, with below-target Swedish inflation and high unemployment allowing it to wait even as imported-price risks could lift its projected path. Norges Bank was expected to hold at 4.25% after its May increase, although sticky inflation made that call less comfortable. The shared prospect of cheaper energy did not eliminate the divergence between weak Swedish domestic pressure and persistent Norwegian inflation.

After the US fixed-income cutoff, Chile’s central bank unanimously held its rate at 4.5% for a fourth meeting. It said inflation risks had moved closer to balance as demand weakened and the fuel-price shock remained contained, while warning that oil supply had not normalized. The bank lowered its 2026 growth forecast to 1%-1.75% from 1.5%-2.5%. Because the decision came after the completed Treasury session, it did not contribute to the June 16 US yield move.

## Primary Markets Stay Open While Stressed Borrowers Seek Time

Sovereign and corporate issuers continued to find financing windows, but the strongest transactions combined clear use of proceeds with either scarcity or explicit concessions. The Philippines raised $2.5 billion in its second and final international bond sale of 2026, increasing the transaction from an initial $2 billion after orders reached 4.4 times the offered amount.

The three-part dollar sale included a $300 million reopening of a bond issued in January. A new 10-year tranche priced 92.5 basis points over Treasuries, compared with initial talk around 125 basis points, while the 5.5-year bond priced at a 55-basis-point spread after guidance began near 85 basis points. The government said the transaction completed its external commercial borrowing for the year.

The deal benefited from improving risk appetite around the prospective US-Iran agreement, but it also highlighted the contrast between external and domestic financing costs. At a Philippine auction of 7-year notes, the average yield rose 13.6 basis points to 6.779%, and the Treasury had rejected bids at recent local sales to restrain borrowing costs. The dollar transaction gave Manila access to tighter relative pricing even as its broader annual borrowing plan remained large at 2.68 trillion pesos.

STMicroelectronics turned a 200% year-to-date share-price rise into cheaper equity-linked funding. The chipmaker planned a $1.5 billion convertible-bond sale in two tranches due in 2031 and 2033. It intended to use part of the proceeds to redeem $750 million of zero-coupon notes due in 2027 and the remainder for general corporate purposes.

The 2031 bonds were marketed with a 0%-0.5% coupon and a conversion premium of 47.5%-52.5%; the 2033 tranche carried a proposed 0.625%-1.125% coupon and a 50%-55% conversion premium. Refinancing the 2027 notes also addresses dilution risk because STMicro’s shares have risen above their $45.10 conversion price. The transaction joined a wave of convertible issuance by companies financing data-center and artificial-intelligence investment at lower cash coupons than straight debt would require.

Not all funding developments reflected market abundance. Indonesian corporate-bond volatility reached its highest in 4 years as government bonds, the rupiah and policy expectations moved sharply. The 30-day annualized volatility of top-rated corporate debt climbed to 23%. Rupiah corporate issuance was still running at a record 76.8 trillion rupiah for the year, up about 11%, but analysts expected some issuers to reduce deal sizes or wait for more stable pricing.

Five-year AAA corporate spreads had widened or tightened by more than 10 basis points on different days during the preceding week. That volatility made it difficult for borrowers and funds to agree on a clearing premium over government debt, even where underlying credit quality had not changed. The local bond market had become more important as the rupiah weakened, leaving higher coupons capable of restraining investment and consumption even if issuance did not stop.

Optimum Communications’ restructuring dispute showed how legal and tax structure can dominate conventional valuation. The company warned creditors that forcing foreclosure or a debt-for-equity exchange at its CSC Holdings unit could trigger more than $4 billion of tax liabilities through deconsolidation. CSC has more than $20 billion of borrowings within Optimum’s roughly $26 billion debt load.

Optimum proposed a consensual restructuring in which CSC creditors would receive equity in the parent, an arrangement the company said could reduce the tax cost. Creditors were still examining whether the threatened liability was credible, with advisers given access to the underlying analysis. The dispute was visible in prices: $1 billion of 7.5% notes due in 2028 fell more than 3 cents on Tuesday to 26 cents, while $2.1 billion of 11.75% bonds due in 2029 stabilized just above 60 cents after trading in the mid-70s 2 months earlier.

Brightline Trains Florida obtained a narrower form of relief. Holders of $985 million of 12% municipal bonds extended a payment due Monday through the end of June and waived a default tied to $22.2 million of new borrowing completed May 21 without their consent. Assured Guaranty, which insures more than $1 billion of senior Brightline bonds, provided the working-capital loan, according to a person familiar with the transaction.

The extension moves the immediate deadline to the same period as July 1 coupon payments on $2.2 billion of senior debt and $1.1 billion of corporate notes. Brightline was considering bankruptcy-financing offers after failing to attract a buyer by a self-imposed deadline. The new money and waiver therefore provided time for a negotiated liability-management process; they did not resolve a $5.5 billion debt burden supported by passenger revenue and earnings that had fallen well short of earlier projections.

A separate conditional financing showed the expanding role of the US government in strategic supply chains. Rare-earth refiner Phoenix Tailings secured a conditional $500 million Pentagon loan for a proposed plant intended to produce several rare-earth materials by 2028. The commitment remains subject to financial, legal and technical due diligence before closing. Together with a recent $66 million Energy Department award, it supports a project aimed at reducing dependence on Chinese processing capacity, but the financing is not yet funded debt.

The day’s credit evidence was consequently selective rather than uniformly strong or weak. The Philippines and STMicro used favorable market conditions to secure substantial funding on improved terms. Indonesian issuers faced price volatility despite record year-to-date volume. Optimum used a disputed tax consequence as restructuring leverage, and Brightline’s creditors exchanged immediate enforcement for more negotiating time. Those distinctions mattered more than the small daily moves in broad credit funds.

## Forward Market Significance

The immediate US focus is May retail sales at 08:30 ET on June 17. Headline sales are expected to rise between 0.4% and 0.6% after a 0.5% April gain, with sales excluding autos and gasoline expected to increase 0.3% and the control group 0.4%. A firm result would contrast with the housing slump and support the view that consumption can tolerate restrictive rates. A weak report would broaden the evidence of softer domestic demand before the Fed decision.

The FOMC announces at 14:00 ET and Warsh holds his first post-meeting press conference at 14:30. An unchanged 3.50%-3.75% target range is widely expected. The market-moving information will be the distribution of rate projections, the treatment of the prior easing bias and the balance Warsh draws between realized goods inflation and the prospective relief from cheaper oil. Any changes to the style or amount of guidance could affect term premium separately from the projected funds-rate path.

UK consumer prices arrive earlier on June 17. Headline inflation is expected to rise 0.4% on the month and 3.0% from a year earlier, after readings of 0.7% and 2.8%. The release is the final major inflation input before the Bank of England’s June 18 decision, where a hold at 3.75% is expected. The vote split and guidance will show whether officials give more weight to softer activity and declining oil or to the inflation expectations and lagged price effects already generated by the energy shock.

Euro-area final inflation is expected to confirm the May flash readings of 3.2% headline and 2.5% core. The outcome will be read alongside the moderation in hourly labor-cost growth to 3.2% and the small quarterly rise in vacancies. Confirmation would leave the ECB balancing a less forceful wage signal against officials’ warnings that food, goods and services inflation will continue absorbing earlier energy costs.

The Riksbank decides June 17, with a hold at 1.75% expected, while Norges Bank follows June 18 and is expected to keep its rate at 4.25%. Sweden’s updated path will show whether imported inflation is enough to bring a future increase closer despite weak domestic conditions. Norway’s path will indicate whether its May increase was a discrete response or part of a further sequence.

June 18 also brings decisions from Bank Indonesia, the Swiss National Bank, the Bank of England and the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. Indonesia and the Philippines are each expected to consider another 25-basis-point increase, while the SNB is expected to hold at 0.00%. Currency stability, domestic demand and the speed of energy-price pass-through leave those decisions more differentiated than the common fall in oil might suggest.

Treasury will auction $70 billion of 4-week bills and $75 billion of 8-week bills at 11:30 ET on June 18. At 13:00 it will reopen $24 billion of 1.250% 5-year TIPS due April 2031. The inflation-protected sale follows the Fed projections and a June 16 session in which the 10-year breakeven fell 3.2 basis points while the real yield barely moved. Its bidding and allocation will provide a direct test of demand for real yield and inflation protection after the oil-driven repricing.

US initial jobless claims on June 18 will update whether the recent increase to 229,000 new claims and 1.795 million continuing claims is becoming persistent. The labor figures are central to the divide between economists expecting eventual cuts and strategists arguing that resilient employment, easy financial conditions and broad inflation will require increases.

Japan releases May national consumer prices on June 19. Inflation excluding fresh food is expected to remain at 1.4% from a year earlier. The first national inflation release after the BOJ’s increase will test its warning that oil pass-through and expectations could push underlying inflation above target, while helping markets judge whether another move by October is plausible.

The proposed US-Iran agreement is also scheduled for signature June 19, when SIFMA recommends a full close for US fixed-income trading. The holiday delays domestic price discovery around the final terms, allied participation in mine clearance and any timetable for resumed shipping. The relevant energy test is not the signature alone, but whether safe passage, production and export volumes recover on the schedule now embedded in lower crude prices.

section_summaries.market_read: The larger decline in breakevens than real yields identified cheaper prospective energy as the main force behind the nominal rally.
section_summaries.summary: The Treasury rally extended beyond the front end as falling crude reduced inflation compensation, weak housing highlighted the damage from restrictive borrowing costs and solid demand for the 20-year reopening supported duration. Import-price pressure nevertheless left the Fed facing realized goods inflation alongside prospective energy relief, while losses in technology shares showed that the decline in oil did not produce a uniform risk rally.

section_summaries.market_read: Lower energy-related inflation compensation and firm auction demand favored the 5- to 30-year sectors over the 2-year.
section_summaries.section_title: Oil Relief Reaches the Long End
section_summaries.summary: The 10- and 30-year sectors joined the rally as a near-final US-Iran accord offered a clearer path to additional oil supply, but the financial repricing ran ahead of physical restoration. European participation in mine clearance remained unsettled, regional tensions persisted and QatarEnergy expected to restore only about half its capacity one month after safe passage resumed. Stronger auction cover and a lower dealer share helped the 20-year sector absorb heavy activity without surrendering its gains.

section_summaries.section_title: Import Inflation and a Housing Slump Complicate the Fed’s Choice
section_summaries.summary: Import prices rose 1.9% in May, with fuel up 12.5% and nonfuel imports up 0.8%, showing that the external inflation impulse had broadened. Housing starts simultaneously fell 15.4% to their weakest annualized pace in 6 years, led by multifamily construction but accompanied by softer single-family activity. The evidence supported a June hold without resolving whether later policy should tighten or ease, while possible changes to Fed communication created a separate term-premium risk.

section_summaries.market_read: Higher long yields and a muted yen response showed doubt that gradual tightening will quickly stabilize prices and the currency.
section_summaries.next_check: May national inflation on June 19 will test the BOJ's pass-through warning and expectations for another increase by October.
section_summaries.section_title: The BOJ Tightens, but the Yen and Long Bonds Question the Pace
section_summaries.summary: The BOJ raised its policy rate 25 basis points to 1% and warned that energy pass-through and inflation expectations could push underlying inflation above target. Yet the yen remained near 160 per dollar and 10- and 20-year government-bond yields rose 7 basis points as markets judged the path of further tightening to be gradual. From April 2027, purchases will remain near ¥2 trillion a month, separating rate normalization from a faster discretionary withdrawal of bond support.

section_summaries.market_read: China's industrial strength has not produced a comparable recovery in consumption, property or broad private investment.
section_summaries.section_title: China Weakens as Europe’s Labor Signals Point in Different Directions
section_summaries.summary: China's May data showed export- and technology-led production diverging further from weak household and private demand: retail sales fell for the first time since the post-pandemic reopening, investment contracted and property prices declined, even as industrial production accelerated. Euro-area labor-cost growth eased to 3.2%, while vacancies edged higher from Q4 but remained below a year earlier, leaving the ECB to balance softer wage pressure against lagged energy effects.

section_summaries.market_read: Strong primary deals reflected clear proceeds and favorable structures, while stressed borrowers secured time rather than resolution.
section_summaries.next_check: Brightline's extension runs through end-June, alongside July 1 payments on senior debt and corporate notes.
section_summaries.section_title: Primary Markets Stay Open While Stressed Borrowers Seek Time
section_summaries.summary: Funding remained available but highly selective. The Philippines expanded a heavily subscribed $2.5 billion dollar sale, and STMicroelectronics used its share-price rise to pursue cheaper convertible financing. Indonesian corporate issuers faced sharp pricing volatility despite record year-to-date volume, while Optimum invoked a disputed tax liability in restructuring talks and Brightline obtained only a temporary extension and waiver. A conditional Pentagon loan for Phoenix Tailings remained subject to due diligence.

The June 17 Fed decision will test how Warsh balances realized goods inflation, cheaper prospective energy and weakening rate-sensitive demand, with communication changes potentially affecting term premium independently of the projected policy path. Subsequent Treasury supply and the proposed US-Iran signing will test whether demand for inflation protection and the restoration of physical energy flows validate the repricing already visible in crude and breakevens.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries Rally as Oil Relief Lowers Inflation Compensation
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied on June 16, with the 2-year yield down 1.4 basis points to 4.055%, the 5-year down 2.8 basis points to 4.164%, the 10-year down 3.5 basis points to 4.44% and the 30-year down 3.6 basis points to 4.944%. The move flattened 2s10s to 38.5 basis points and 2s30s to 88.9 basis points.

Lower inflation compensation drove almost all of the long-end move. The 10-year breakeven fell 3.2 basis points to 2.306%, while the 10-year real yield slipped only 0.3 basis point to 2.134%, as WTI fell 5.82% and Brent dropped 5.06%. A near-final US-Iran agreement contemplated immediate Iranian oil sales, but the proposed June 19 signing did not settle when safe passage, production and exports would recover.

US data complicated the policy outlook. Housing starts plunged 15.4% to a 1.18 million annualized rate, while import prices rose 1.9%, including a broad 0.8% increase outside fuel. A $13 billion 20-year reopening drew stronger cover and a low dealer share, helping duration hold its gains. Equities fell, especially semiconductors, and volatility rose, leaving risk appetite selective before Kevin Warsh's first Fed decision as chair.
overall_summary.summary: Treasuries rallied and the curve flattened as another sharp drop in oil reduced inflation compensation, weak housing construction reinforced concern about rate-sensitive demand and a well-absorbed 20-year reopening supported the long end, while broad import-price pressure kept the Fed from receiving an inflation all-clear.
